topic: Loudest animal: sperm whale echolocation clicks measured at source levels up to 236 dB re 1 µPa (pp) at 1 m by Møhl et al. 2003 (JASA), recorded off Andenes, northern Norway, with a hydrophone array; monopulsed clicks ~100 µs long from the spermaceti organ (the whale's enormous nose). Blue whale calls 188–191 dB re 1 µPa (Frontiers in Marine Science 2021). Howler monkeys: loudest land animal, ~140 dB in air, audible ~5 km (Current Biology 2015; Nat Geo). Sperm whales dive beyond 2,000 m hunting squid, navigating by echolocation. Underwater and in-air decibels are not directly comparable; the on-screen bars say so.
policy_note: Every spoken or shown fact → a claim with ≥ 2 independent publishers; core claims need a primary/scholarly source.
